questions.question: S, T, U, V, W and X are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). W sits second to the right of U. T sits second to the right of W. X sits to the immediate right of T. Who sits to the immediate right of X?
questions.solution:
Given, S, T, U, V, W, and X are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order).

W sits second to the right of U.

T sits second to the right of W.

X sits to the immediate right of T.

So from above, U sits to the immediate right of X.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2".

questions.question:
10 is related to 102 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 13 is related to 171. To which of the following is 16 related, following the same logic?

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g., 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding / subtracting / multiplying, etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic: If x is the first number and y is the second number, then y = x² + 2.

Now,

For 10 is related to 102:

⇒ 10² + 2 = 100 + 2 = 102.

For 13 is related to 171:

⇒ 13² + 2 = 169 + 2 = 171.

Similarly, for 16:

⇒ 16² + 2 = 256 + 2 = 258.

So, 16 is related to **258**.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3".

questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

Some actors are dancers.

Some dancers are singers.

**Conclusions:**

(I) Some actors are singers.

(II) No singer is a dancer.

options.text: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow

questions.solution:
Given Statements:

Some actors are dancers.

Some dancers are singers.

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/12de6c6cf43d65e74d6f0af3a3dec561e6032b810fb135c7ff4a000c20813f5f.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some actors are singers - **False** (There is no direct logical connection established between actors and singers from the given statements. It is a possibility, but not a definite conclusion.)

II. No singer is a dancer - **False** (The statement "Some dancers are singers" directly contradicts this conclusion. Since some dancers are singers, it means there is an overlap, and therefore, it's not possible that no singer is a dancer.)

So, Neither conclusion I nor conclusion II follows.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 2"**.

questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements**

 
• Some creepers are stones.
 
• Some stones are buds.

**Conclusions:**

 
• Some buds are stones.
 
• No creeper is a bud.
questions.solution:
Given Statements:

Some creepers are stones.

Some stones are buds.

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b3a0d5ed4b5384ebfcf64f54e4f81cd8123a574bcf00d6d8be57d13f555f004f.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some buds are stones - **True** (This is a direct converse of the statement "Some stones are buds". If some stones are buds, then it logically follows that some buds are stones.)

II. No creeper is a bud - **False** (There is no direct relationship or definite exclusion established between creepers and buds in the statements.Therefore, "No creeper is a bud" cannot be definitively concluded.)

So, Only conclusion I follows.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 3"**.

questions.question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)

**(16, 3, 27)

(10, 19, 37)**
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic: In each set (A, B, C), the pattern is: C = A + B + 8

Now,

For (16, 3, 27):

⇒ 16 + 3 + 8 = 19 + 8 = 27.

For (10, 19, 37):

⇒ 10 + 19 + 8 = 29 + 8 = 37.

Similarly, let's check the options:

1) (5, 14, 20)

⇒ 5 + 14 + 8 = 19 + 8 = 27 ≠ 20 (Incorrect)

2) (15, 17, 30)

⇒ 15 + 17 + 8 = 32 + 8 = 40 ≠ 30 (Incorrect)

3) (19, 15, 32)

⇒ 19 + 15 + 8 = 34 + 8 = 42 ≠ 32 (Incorrect)

**4) (7, 25, 40)**

**⇒ 7 + 25 + 8 = 32 + 8 = 40 (Correct)**

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 4"**.
